criteria.evidence: Within the classical R boundary, §§1.7, 9.3, 17.1–17.6 and 18.1/18.6 identify the materialised classical state, ordinary reversible runtime memory, source counters and ISA history. ISA §§4.9/7.4/10 determine one terminal record, intact open activations and eligible FAILED reversal. The new text preserves these distinctions.

suggestions: S1, rung 3, evidence: retain the packet's explicit separation between contract acceptance and implementation readiness. For the eventual rung-3 receipt, compile formatted-console.c through the actual plugin and linked musl vfprintf on LLVM 18 and 23, run each object on both executors, require exactly hex 7879202d372039203261205a20303030313220616263 with no added newline, then reset and replay. Include normal return, explicit exit, _Exit and a fault with a pending stdio buffer; cleanup must follow §§11.2/19.2 exactly once, and the fault must preserve its prefix without flushing. Record materialisation, runtime, object, build-record and executor identities. This is a readiness recommendation, not a prerequisite for accepting the specification.

S1, §§11.2/18.6, rung 3: add an explicit zero-length boundary example to distinguish syscall framing from direct effect markers. Suggested wording: "A zero-length console syscall emits no effect under the syscall framing rule; an explicitly executed zero-length effect marker still follows ISA §7.3 and contributes an effect/journal entry." With a valid pointer 4096 and length 0, the latter entry is {"args":[4096,0],"bytes":"","dev":"console","op":"write"}. This preserves the already mandatory direct marker-to-ISA mapping and prevents applying the syscall optimisation to arbitrary ISA effects.

S1, §18.6, rung 3: extend the saved-tape tests beyond the two console writes to memory-writing clock/entropy/block effects, cancellation, a requested forward prefix and FAILED reversal. Include extra keys, odd/nonhex bytes, integer threshold encodings and repeated CLI options. Expected behavior remains the existing rule: reject malformed input as a tool error, reject a candidate before mutation/cursor advance, retain the earlier committed prefix, and emit neither success JSON nor tape output on replay error.

path_to_accept: No blocking changes required. Ruling 1: accept 0.3-r1 as the distinct full compatibility identity for the explicitly graded classical R applicability and its CC launch stub; this does not accept the full 0.3 draft or weaken its ungraded obligations. Ruling 2: the fault table agrees with ISA §§4.9/5.4/10: zero becomes 4, all nonzero u64 causes survive, exhausted source instructions fault before execution, results and caller successors are absent, the successful prefix remains intact, and eligible FAILED reversal undoes it. Ruling 3: the exact plugin/options/module flag plus checked JCS build-record digest are sufficient; map remains 0.3, ISA-owned fields retain their meaning, and migration requires recomputed objects and dependent bindings. Ruling 4: accept the console lifecycle: fd liveness and buffers are reversible runtime memory, closing one descriptor leaves the other sink binding usable, normal main return follows exit cleanup exactly once, and terminal faults do not flush. Ruling 5: adopt saved-tape-v1 as mandatory for this profile at the tool boundary, with strict journal validation before effect commit, retained cancelled effects, separate active tape, trailing-input rejection and explicit tool errors. To raise C6 from 4 to 5, add the state-observing transactional replay witness and identity-bound producer/musl/both-executor rung-3 receipt described in the suggestions; their absence is not a false semantic statement or a scope narrowing.
summary: Accept the classical R-contract profile 0.3-r1 at frozen candidate 0822cbc; verdict_core=accept, no confirmed S0 blocker and no identified regression from the supplied diff. Typed terminal faults, console cleanup, compatibility metadata and the saved-journal/active-tape distinction match the cited ISA contracts. The mixed native/device object remains reachable. Independently reran the finite R family (4/4) and focused r-contract/header/inventory/xrefs/lowering selection (1571/1571) with headless environment, timeout, immutable interpreter and scratch redirected to tmp-sol; tracked snapshot remains clean. These checks and this verdict do not establish whole-0.3 acceptance, production musl compilation, transactional private-state coverage or completion of rung 3 on both executors. All five requested rulings are affirmative within the stated boundary.
